name: a5
description: Group geographic points into A5 pentagonal cells in DuckDB. Use cell IDs to count points by area, join datasets, or roll up to a coarser grid.

cta.title: Spatial bucketing with pentagonal cells
cta.description: Install A5 to index points by uniform-area pentagonal cells inside DuckDB — useful when H3's hex-area variation (it swings by roughly 2× across the globe, not just near the poles) is a problem for your aggregation.

quickStart.title: Put two nearby points in grid cells
quickStart.description: The sample includes two New York coordinates. A5 takes longitude first, then latitude; resolution controls cell size.
quickStart.sql:
WITH points(longitude, latitude) AS (
  VALUES (-74.0060, 40.7128), (-74.0061, 40.7129)
)
SELECT a5_lonlat_to_cell(longitude, latitude, 10) AS cell_id,
       count(*) AS point_count
FROM points
GROUP BY cell_id
ORDER BY cell_id;
quickStart.note: These points fall in one cell, giving a point count of 2. The numeric cell ID differs between A5 builds: check the [migration notes](#cell-ids-from-earlier-versions) before combining stored IDs. Cell membership is a grid approximation; use an exact geometry predicate when a boundary matters.

introduction.title: Group geographic points into equal-area cells
paragraphs: A5 divides the globe into a hierarchy of pentagonal cells. The extension converts longitude and latitude into a cell ID, so locations can be grouped and joined using an integer instead of a pair of coordinates.

Use it to count events by area, compare geographic densities, or summarize a detailed grid at a coarser resolution. Cells at the same resolution have equal area. You can turn a cell back into a polygon when you need to draw it on a map.
